obligation: Bank recall request for a diverted payment
trigger: A payment (ACH or wire) is suspected to have gone to an account controlled by an attacker
deadline: Immediately on suspicion. IC3: 'time is of the essence'; request a recall and any indemnification documents
notify: The company's bank fraud line (outbound payments); ask the client to call its own bank (inbound payments)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - practical step, not a legal duty. First action in this runbook

obligation: Complaint to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
trigger: Any business email compromise with a fraudulent transfer or attempt
deadline: As soon as possible, regardless of the amount; IC3 may help freeze funds

trigger: Unauthorized access to personal information of Florida residents. Includes name plus Social Security number, or an email address plus the password that opens the account (501.171(1)(g)). Fla. Stat. 501.171 covers sole proprietorships
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (law enforcement delay allowed on written request; 15 more days if good cause for delay is given in writing to the Department within the 30 days, 501.171(3)(a))
notify: Each affected Florida resident (mail or email)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the mailbox or accounting SaaS held subcontractors' W-9 forms with Social Security numbers (8 sole-proprietor subcontractors)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - fewer than 30 people's personal information is held

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
applies_at_this_tier: No - fewer than 30 people's personal information is held

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (instead of individual notice)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or financial harm
deadline: Document in writing; keep 5 years; give to the Department within 30 days after the determination

obligation: Vendor (third-party agent) breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (accounting SaaS, email provider, bookkeeper) has a breach
deadline: Vendor must notify the company no later than 10 days after its determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - add to the bookkeeper engagement letter; check SaaS terms

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected subcontractors live

obligation: Correct SAM EFT information and alert the federal payment office
trigger: The company's EFT (bank) information in SAM was changed without authorization, or the FC-1 payment is missing
deadline: Immediately. If EFT information was incorrect or revised within 30 days of the Government's release of payment and the funds have left the payment office, the Government is deemed to have paid and the company must recover the funds
notify: SAM (correct the record); FC-1 Contracting Officer and paying office

obligation: Pay FC-1 subcontractors despite a diverted payment
trigger: A payment meant for an FC-1 subcontractor went to an attacker
deadline: Subcontractor must still be paid within 7 days of the company's receipt of the Government's payment; interest penalty if late
notify: The subcontractor (after call-back to the number in its subcontract)

obligation: Report discovery of covered telecommunications equipment or services during contract performance
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered equipment identified in a system during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; mitigation details within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered by business email compromise. Listed because FC-1 includes the clause (used in July 2026 for the hotspot)

obligation: Report a Kaspersky covered article provided to the Government
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: A Kaspersky covered article identified during contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Not expected: the owner provides no software or network equipment on FC-1

obligation: DoD cyber incident reporting for covered defense information
trigger: Cyber incident affecting a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery ('rapidly report'); preserve images 90 days; subcontractors report to DoD and give incident number to the prime
notify: DoD via https://dibnet.dod.mil (DoD-approved medium assurance certificate required); malware to DoD Cyber Crime Center (DC3)
applies_at_this_tier: No - no DoD contract today and no covered defense information (P03 G-032). Recheck when the DoD subcontract is signed

obligation: CMMC status currency after an incident
trigger: An incident shows that a CMMC Level 1 requirement is no longer met
deadline: Before relying on the status for the DoD subcontract or making the next annual affirmation; restore compliance and re-assess
notify: Owner as Affirming Official; tell the prime contractor if the status is no longer current
applies_at_this_tier: After the owner holds Final Level 1 (Self), expected 2026-11-30. The clause has no separate incident notice duty

obligation: Client notice of a compromised payment channel
trigger: Any sign that a client received false remittance instructions from the company's mailbox or a lookalike domain
deadline: Immediately by phone to the client contact in the contract, then in writing
notify: Each client with an open pay app; the VA paying office for FC-1
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and practical, not a statutory duty

trigger: Suspected security incident or funds transfer fraud
applies_at_this_tier: No cyber or social engineering coverage today. Tell the insurance agent anyway, and ask whether the general liability or a crime policy responds

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (not in effect). Construction is not a CISA critical infrastructure sector; recheck when final

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Not for business email compromise (no ransom). Applies only if an extortion demand follows
